senses.gloss: m. (גדד, v. גַּד I) worm-wood, bitter herb.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Amos 5:7">Targ. Am. V, 7</cite>.

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 5:4">Targ. Prov. V, 4</cite> <he>גידדא</he> ed. Lag. (ed. <he>גיררא</he>, <cite ref="C00809"><he>גירא</he></cite>, corr. acc.; Ar. <cite ref="C00645"><he>גִּידֵּי</he></cite> pl.).—Pl. <cite ref="C00765"><he>גִּידִּין</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 9:14">Targ. Jer. IX, 14</cite> Ar. (ed. <he>גירין</he>, corr. acc.). Ib. XXIII, 15; a. e.—(In h. diction) <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 126">Yalk. Gen. 126</cite>, v. <cite ref="C00153"><he>גַּד</he> I</cite>. Tanḥ. B’shall., ed. Bub. 22 (play on <cite ref="C00151"><he>גד</he></cite>) <he>שהיה בפיהם כג׳ מרין</he> the manna was in their (the gentiles’) mouths like bitter worm-wood.

<cite ref="Shabbat 87a:8">Sabb. 87ᵃ</cite> (play on <he>ויג̇ד̇</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 19:9">Ex. XIX, 9</cite>) <he>דברים שקשין לאדם כגִֹידִֹּין</he> words (of warning against punishment) which are as hard (distasteful) to man as worm-wood. [<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 49:23">Targ. Y. I Gen. XLIX, 23</cite>, <cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 49:23">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XLIX, 23</cite> <he>גידין</he>, <he>גידיא</he> some ed., read <he>גיר׳</he>, v. <cite ref="C00806"><he>גִּיר</he> III</cite>.]
